stem:
Farid must construct a $90^\circ$ angle at point $T$ on a given straight line.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Mark points $X$ and $Y$ on the line at equal distances from $T$ so that $T$ is the midpoint of $XY$, then construct the perpendicular bisector of $XY$.
Keep $T$ on the line, but skip making $T$ the midpoint of a segment on that line.
First draw a $60^\circ$ angle at $T$ by an equilateral triangle, then halve it to get $30^\circ$.
Treat $T$ as a point outside the line and drop a perpendicular from outside.

teacher.key_rationale: Make T the midpoint of XY on the line, then the perpendicular bisector of XY is the 90° line at T. Skipping the midpoint omits the needed condition. Building 60°/30° conflates another construction. Treating T as outside changes the scope.
